requirements.title: Versioned complete replay inputs with effect isolation
requirements.ears: WHEN a reducer replay is evaluated, the verifier SHALL reproduce state and ordered effect descriptions from versioned initial state and complete recorded inputs, reject invalid input explicitly, report selected and processed coverage, and execute no native mutations.

scenarios.name: Deterministic history
scenarios.given: A valid checkpoint and ordered native observations including deadlines
scenarios.when: The compiled reducer processes them twice
scenarios.then: All state/effect rows match and no effect endpoint is invoked

scenarios.name: Malformed racing clock input
scenarios.given: A pending request and envelope missing clock-domain metadata
scenarios.when: A late receipt is supplied through the envelope
scenarios.then: Validation fails explicitly; valid inputs retain original deadline and recorded order

requirements.tradeoffs: Fixture/schema upkeep and log bytes; preserve existing reducer rather than build another. Recorded timer inputs do not qualify native deadlines.
requirements.guardrails: Sanitized replay needs an explicit semantics-preserving mapping. Refused dummy events are counted explicitly; a nonempty selected corpus cannot pass by processing zero inputs.

requirements.title: Proof-safe bounded history retention and compaction
requirements.ears: WHEN retained records reach their configured bound, the authority SHALL reclaim only records whose obligations remain protected by proofs and replay floors, or report distinct capacity refusal while preserving unresolved and cleanup obligations until proof-safe reclamation permits admission.

scenarios.name: Expired replay after compaction
scenarios.given: A settled reclaimable record and retained replay floor
scenarios.when: Compaction completes and its old identity returns
scenarios.then: no mutation occurs; expired or retention disposition is distinct from definitive refusal of the original operation, and retained Unknown remains unchanged

scenarios.name: Unknown and late cleanup
scenarios.given: Capacity pressure, Unknown request and outstanding consumer fence
scenarios.when: Diagnostics rotate and matching late receipt arrives
scenarios.then: Unresolved/cleanup obligations remain reconciled and charged storage is not freed prematurely

requirements.tradeoffs: Retention ownership table and compaction proof work; persistent sharing cannot make retained roots free; diagnostics may rotate independently.
requirements.guardrails: No age-based deletion of Unknown, cleanup, issuance/revocation authority or replay floors. A presentation close/restart is not proof-safe reclamation. Capacity refusal is distinct from the original operation outcome and clears when proof-safe reclamation is possible. Scope replay floors retire only through authority-certified scope retirement or equivalent retained proof.

requirements.title: Coherent recovery checkpoints and interrupted migration qualification
requirements.ears: WHEN recovery installs a checkpoint, the authority SHALL validate its coherent schema, lifetime, watermark and retained obligations before effect admission, reconcile uncertain outcomes without replay, and preserve each original deadline.

scenarios.name: Completed checkpoint
scenarios.given: Synchronized checkpoint with Unknown and retired-request floors
scenarios.when: Frontend restarts
scenarios.then: Coherent observation/reconciliation state is restored without old mutation dispatch

scenarios.name: Interrupted migration
scenarios.given: Visible rename and incomplete synchronization/migration barrier
scenarios.when: Recovery sees newer scene plus late old-binding receipt
scenarios.then: Validated recovery completes or remains fail-closed without mixed owners, lost Unknown, or reset deadline

requirements.tradeoffs: Crash-barrier fixture maintenance and synchronous storage cost; a manifest over existing stores may suffice; database replacement is deferred.
requirements.guardrails: Use existing durable ledger. Interrupted migration/write/fsync and storage-full are qualifying faults; coherent checkpoint is not proof that a window action completed.

requirements.title: Measured revision-bound derived caching
requirements.ears: WHERE derived-state caching is enabled, the frontend SHALL return the same projection as uncached derivation for every accepted revision and invalidate cached results before using changed or retired dependencies.

scenarios.name: Unchanged dependency
scenarios.given: Pointer events with unchanged scene/query/policy revisions
scenarios.when: Taskbar groups are derived
scenarios.then: output equals the uncached oracle under the correct dependency revision; recomputation and whole-process resource results are measured separately for the adoption decision

scenarios.name: Identity reuse race
scenarios.given: Cached retired family incarnation
scenarios.when: Same label appears under new lifetime/incarnation during query change
scenarios.then: New identities govern derivation and action eligibility; stale family/preview authority does not survive

requirements.tradeoffs: Cache/index memory and invalidation bookkeeping may outweigh scan savings; adoption requires frozen-budget evidence, no invented thresholds.
requirements.guardrails: Caching/indexing is an implementation option after profiling. Cache keys include native dependency/output/publication revisions; stale cached data grants no authority. Enable an optimization only after the frozen workload comparison shows an accepted benefit; equivalence alone does not justify adopting it.

requirements.title: Explicit concrete state and command refinement mapping
requirements.ears: WHEN coupled replay is reported as conformance evidence, the verifier SHALL compare concrete state and ordered commands through a documented abstraction map and disclose stuttering, equivalence and environmental assumptions without substituting that evidence for native acceptance.

scenarios.name: Backend stuttering
scenarios.given: Broker housekeeping without observable frontend change
scenarios.when: Coupled replay applies declared abstraction map
scenarios.then: Frontend stutters while native accounting and eligible queued receipts remain checked

scenarios.name: Equal final state with incorrect effect order
scenarios.given: Executions with equal final visible model
scenarios.when: One reorders Cancel/Ack or retires before consumer completion
scenarios.then: Transition/command/resource comparison fails at first relevant mismatch

scenarios.name: unlisted-field-mutation
scenarios.given: a runtime mutant drops an Unknown reservation or changes an undeclared field
scenarios.when: abstraction coverage and coupled replay run
scenarios.then: verification fails at that field rather than silently observing only the visible model

requirements.tradeoffs: Mapping/comparator reviewer upkeep; full mechanized proof deferred; sampled exploration remains bounded evidence.
requirements.guardrails: Explicit partial-observation/stuttering abstraction; compare actual commands and resources as well as model state. Bounded sampling/trace validation is not an exhaustive proof. Every concrete state and command field is listed as mapped or explicitly reviewed quotient/stutter/ghost-only; an unlisted field fails coverage. Quotients preserve authentication/binding identity, clock/deadline and outcome meaning; reviewed opaque-nonce renaming is allowed without erasing those relations.
scenarioIDs: ELM-ADOPT-005 Equal final state with incorrect effect order

requirements.title: Complete typed internal boundaries
requirements.ears: WHEN a validated external event enters an internal reducer, the controller SHALL carry domain-specific typed identities and outcomes through its resulting effect descriptions until wire encoding.

scenarios.name: Exact receipt
scenarios.given: a validated receipt for one request/incarnation
scenarios.when: the typed outcome is reduced
scenarios.then: only the exact transaction settles and wire encoding remains unchanged

scenarios.name: Foreign input
scenarios.given: a malformed, untrusted or unauthorized payload that fails boundary admission
scenarios.when: boundary validation runs
scenarios.then: no admitted event, native mutation or transaction settlement is produced; only a bounded allowlisted rejection diagnostic is retained, with no fabricated Refused outcome

scenarios.name: authenticated-historical-reconciliation
scenarios.given: an exact authenticated historical receipt for a retained obligation and its declared reconciliation route
scenarios.when: it arrives after frontend replacement
scenarios.then: only the historical obligation may settle; the receipt grants no authority to the replacement binding and renews no deadline

requirements.tradeoffs: Codec and call-site migration; phantom types do not authenticate senders; preserve wire bytes.
requirements.guardrails: Narrow module-owned typed events, effects and identity domains; native authenticates context. Do not mandate a new language, framework, giant event type or incompatible wire change. Terminal Refused requires exact authenticated native evidence or a validated definitive unsent certificate. Historical proof admission follows its explicit recovery contract.

requirements.title: Preserve effects as an auditable dependency algebra
requirements.ears: WHEN a native effect depends on a prerequisite, the controller SHALL admit its request only after matching authenticated evidence satisfies that operation's protocol-specific prerequisite, while native authority revalidates the dependency at commit.

scenarios.name: Pending prerequisite
scenarios.given: restore-before-activate dependency for an exact incarnation
scenarios.when: restore remains Pending then its exact committed receipt arrives
scenarios.then: activation waits then registered activation can proceed

scenarios.name: Wrong prerequisite
scenarios.given: a refused restore or foreign committed receipt
scenarios.when: it arrives before activation
scenarios.then: it cannot satisfy the prerequisite and independent controls remain usable

requirements.tradeoffs: Explicit dependency metadata and replay oracle costs; retain independence; no new framework necessary.
requirements.guardrails: Register every implied native request; preserve child effects. Cmd.batch does not sequence dependent results. Independent actions need not wait for unrelated dependencies. Native revalidates prerequisite incarnation, generation and dependency revision. Preview drain/release/presentation require their own evidence; a window Committed receipt cannot substitute.

requirements.title: Publish one conversation contract with local obligations
requirements.ears: WHEN a protocol event is received, each participant SHALL admit it only under the declared actor-specific transitions, version and outcome reachability with exact correlation; otherwise it SHALL reject it without authority, ownership or settlement effect and retain a bounded rejection diagnostic.

scenarios.name: Unadopted refusal
scenarios.given: an admitted reservation without storage
scenarios.when: the trusted producer refuses
scenarios.then: stable refusal proof preserves already-ordered cancellation proof

scenarios.name: Illegal retirement
scenarios.given: an adopted buffer or stale actor
scenarios.when: producer-refused or final-ack is supplied
scenarios.then: it cannot bypass drainage or retire current actor resource

requirements.tradeoffs: New verification artifact refining existing behavior; manual table maintenance; no static-session-typing claim.
requirements.guardrails: Share semantic outcome classes but keep operation/protocol-specific transitions. Window Committed is not preview Released/fenced/presented. Model transitions/typestate are implementation choices, not a claim of static session typing.

requirements.title: Treat cancellation as a request followed by proved closure
requirements.ears: WHILE a resource or reservation is owned, the native broker SHALL account for its admission, transfer and cleanup until matching native completion permits retirement; cancellation or release intent alone SHALL NOT erase ownership, charge or cleanup obligations.

scenarios.name: Cancel refusal race
scenarios.given: capture cancelled before adoption
scenarios.when: refusal completes asynchronously
scenarios.then: ordered cancellation/refusal proofs leave no reservation after final ack

scenarios.name: Held reader
scenarios.given: adopted buffer with held GIO reader
scenarios.when: cancel and shutdown occur
scenarios.then: fetch revoked immediately and terminal release waits for producer completion and reader drainage

requirements.tradeoffs: Retained records and native callback coordination; release on cancel-send unsafe; generation-scoped drain avoids global waits.
requirements.guardrails: Conservation includes newly admitted resources and ownership transfers. Cancel/Release emission is not physical retirement; producer refusal is valid only after trusted failure before image adoption. Native producer/consumer completion and reader drain remain distinct.

requirements.title: Separate causal order, epoch identity and deadline time
requirements.ears: WHEN queueing, frontend replacement or reconciliation occurs, the authority SHALL preserve the operation's original native clock domain, time origin and deadline while validating ordered control delivery independently of observation revisions.

scenarios.name: Restart receipt
scenarios.given: pending work and frontend restart
scenarios.when: exact late receipt arrives
scenarios.then: original request reconciles without deadline renewal or mutation replay

scenarios.name: Gap clock
scenarios.given: control sequence gap or replaced clock domain
scenarios.when: later delta/timeout arrives
scenarios.then: new admission withheld until coherent reconciliation and invalid timing cannot authorize work

requirements.tradeoffs: Metadata and clock/queue instrumentation; frontend timers may provide feedback or fail-closed withdrawal of unsent local intent, but cannot authorize, extend, settle or time native work or substitute for native original deadlines. Vector clocks are unnecessary.
requirements.guardrails: Original absolute native deadlines/start events survive queue/recovery. Causality/order counters, presentation clock, input clock and epoch are distinct. Late receipts may reconcile knowledge without becoming timely success.

requirements.title: preserve uncertainty in a structured reporting contract
requirements.ears: WHEN an operation report is presented, the shell SHALL derive its message and available recovery actions from a validated correlated outcome and SHALL distinguish definitive refusal from Unknown without implying completion or authorizing replay.

scenarios.name: ERR-01-01
scenarios.given: an admitted restore with lost receipt
scenarios.when: transport disconnects
scenarios.then: the report states that completion is unconfirmed, preserves Unknown and offers no automatic repeat.

scenarios.name: ERR-01-02
scenarios.given: an exact unsent certificate and a simultaneous late receipt for a different request
scenarios.when: reports are reduced
scenarios.then: refusal is attached only to the certified request and the foreign receipt cannot alter its message or actions.

requirements.tradeoffs: status-only messages are cheaper but obscure safe recovery; raw native messages reduce mapping work but leak details and blur semantics. Cost: category registry, compatibility review and differential fixtures. Validation: enumerate every existing outcome/recovery reason; every class has reviewed text and enabled-action oracle; corrupt or future reasons fail closed without fabricating a terminal outcome.
requirements.guardrails: Stable bounded outcome/reason catalog and actionable, reviewed text from a catalog that supports localization. Unknown remains perceivable. Unknown reason within a validated Refused class may use generic refusal text; unknown schema/outcome cannot fabricate Refused. Supporting localization does not add a translation release gate.

requirements.title: one announcement owner and outcome-aware deduplication
requirements.ears: WHEN an eligible correlated outcome transition requires attention, the controller SHALL publish one accessible status through the designated announcement owner, retain focus and suppress repeats of that outcome while preserving later distinct outcome transitions.

scenarios.name: ERR-02-01
scenarios.given: bar and popup projections on two outputs with stable focus
scenarios.when: the same refusal receipt is delivered repeatedly and a popup recreates
scenarios.then: one eligible announcement occurs and recovery detail remains reachable.

scenarios.name: ERR-02-02
scenarios.given: Unknown was announced and the original deadline has elapsed
scenarios.when: a valid late correlated receipt settles knowledge
scenarios.then: a distinct policy-eligible update is exposed without restarting the effect or changing its deadline; unauthenticated, unrelated or unauthorized receipts cause no update, while exact authenticated historical evidence may reconcile retained Unknown through the declared recovery route

requirements.tradeoffs: per-view live regions are simple locally but duplicate output on multiple surfaces; one modal per failure interferes with focus and ordinary work. Cost: semantic routing, native AT integration and multi-output transcript qualification. Validation: count announcements against distinct eligible transitions, observe focus and speech/braille, include duplicate receipts and surface recreation. Preserve existing policy thresholds; freeze any missing quantitative oracle through S02/P0 rather than inventing one.
requirements.guardrails: One announcement owner; deduplicate repeated outcomes, not distinct later state changes. Native speech/braille/focus transcript required; ARIA alone is insufficient. The semantic owner is the controller; delivery must reach a qualified AT-active document or declared native/fallback route, including when application focus remains outside shell.

requirements.title: bounded allowlisted diagnostics independent of authority
requirements.ears: WHILE ordinary diagnostics are enabled, the diagnostics subsystem SHALL admit only allowlisted bounded records and SHALL report record loss without collecting excluded content or altering native authority, operation outcomes or deadlines.

scenarios.name: ERR-03-01
scenarios.given: a decoder failure containing a secret canary and window title
scenarios.when: a diagnostic record is produced
scenarios.then: only allowed category/context fields appear and neither canary nor title is retained.

scenarios.name: ERR-03-02
scenarios.given: diagnostic capacity is exhausted during a pending effect
scenarios.when: further records arrive and a terminal receipt races
scenarios.then: loss is observable, memory stays within the frozen budget and receipt settlement is identical to diagnostics-disabled execution.

requirements.tradeoffs: unrestricted verbose logs simplify one incident at privacy/resource cost; aggregate-only metrics lose sequence context. Cost: event schema, producer audits and saturation tests. A ring buffer and separate counters are possible implementations, not mandated architecture. Validation: sensitive canaries across nested values and error strings; resource saturation, failure to write and malformed events preserve controller decisions. Measure log-rate, whole-process CPU/wakeups/memory, export cost and retention against `elm-performance/spec.md` ELM-QA-021/023 and ELM-REV-020/021; the performance owner freezes numeric limits from P0 workloads before acceptance. Measure under the actual ELM-QA-021/023 and ELM-REV-020/021 budget contract.
requirements.guardrails: Secrets, credentials, draft contents and captured pixels are always excluded from ordinary diagnostics under ELM-DEL-017. Raw port bodies, titles, arguments and paths are also excluded by this ordinary allowlist. A different scoped mode requires a separate reviewed contract and is outside this draft. Retention/loss counters remain bounded. Saturation cannot block native control/cleanup or compact durable authority.

requirements.title: recovery evidence distinguishes restored availability from past success
requirements.ears: WHEN a failed frontend or authority recovers, the shell SHALL report verified current availability separately from unresolved historical outcomes and SHALL admit new effects only after native reconciliation under the original deadline and identity contracts.

scenarios.name: ERR-04-01
scenarios.given: an admitted effect and crash before durable settlement
scenarios.when: a fresh epoch receives a coherent snapshot
scenarios.then: availability may recover while the previous effect remains unconfirmed and is never replayed.

scenarios.name: ERR-04-02
scenarios.given: a storage-full recovery failure and matching-looking geometry from a replacement incarnation
scenarios.when: reconciliation is attempted
scenarios.then: geometry alone cannot clear the historical reservation, no new dependent effect is admitted and each affected operation's original deadline is unchanged and is not renewed by recovery.

requirements.tradeoffs: automatic retries may appear faster but are prohibited here; generic “recovered” banners omit the critical uncertainty. Cost: recovery phase/report integration and protected fault campaign evidence. Validation: original restore38/recovery34 with unchanged identity/oracle/deadline, held effects, missing/corrupt journal, unavailable storage, frontend/authority epoch replacement and stale proof. Component replay supplements rather than replaces native acceptance.
requirements.guardrails: Recovery action must preserve durable Unknown, replay floors, held resources and original clocks. Generic restart guidance is not acceptance. Compositor replacement is not an incidental recovery action.

requirements.title: explicit diagnostics export boundary
requirements.ears: WHERE local diagnostic export is selected, WHEN the user requests an export, the shell SHALL produce an inspectable local bundle of validated export-allowed evidence and declared omissions, preserving recovery authority and sending nothing externally.

scenarios.name: ERR-05-01
scenarios.given: diagnostics and an available core dump containing private memory
scenarios.when: the user requests the ordinary bundle
scenarios.then: the bundle includes allowed metadata and states that core/pixels/content are omitted.

scenarios.name: ERR-05-02
scenarios.given: export is assembling records while frontend epoch changes
scenarios.when: cancellation or disk-full occurs
scenarios.then: no success is reported, partial-artifact disposition is explicit, and neither old nor fresh recovery reservation is changed.

requirements.tradeoffs: copying a journal manually is cheaper but produces unreviewable privacy and scope surprises; automated cloud uploads introduce unsupported product scope. Cost: bundle builder, accessible review and export fault testing. Validation: unpack and schema-check artifacts; canary and content scans; stale-epoch snapshot race, cancellation, disk-full and symlink/path defenses; measured export overhead must meet frozen performance budgets.
requirements.guardrails: Conditional/deferrable feature; not a new mandatory release blocker. No default cores, screenshots, environment, unrestricted journals or uploads. Explicit local user request; cancellation/disk-full has truthful partial-artifact outcome.

requirements.title: Preserve control identity across publication and focus changes
requirements.ears: WHILE a shell focus scope is open, the host SHALL preserve an eligible focused control through unrelated publications and dispatch admitted keyboard or assistive activation only to that native AT-exposed identity, rejecting retired or changed-scope targets and applying the frozen fallback when focus becomes ineligible.

scenarios.name: SOL04-01-scenario-1
scenarios.given: Close is focused while another row is selected
scenarios.when: an unrelated catalog publication arrives
scenarios.then: Close keeps focus and the next activation invokes only Close

scenarios.name: SOL04-01-scenario-2
scenarios.given: an activation press belongs to a window incarnation and lease
scenarios.when: that incarnation retires and the row position is reused before release
scenarios.then: release dispatches no replacement action and eligible fallback remains reachable

scenarios.name: focus-without-publication
scenarios.given: Close has keyboard/native AT focus while another row is selected
scenarios.when: Enter or Space is admitted without an intervening publication
scenarios.then: only Close is invoked, no window intent is dispatched and selection cannot override focused identity

requirements.tradeoffs: Identity propagation and native focus evidence; preserve identity rather than index or automatic selected-row refocus.
requirements.guardrails: Publication, lease and incarnation captured at press remain authoritative at release. Preserve the surviving focused identity while eligible under the frozen per-surface policy; disabled-but-focusable controls remain focused when030 allows it, otherwise apply the declared fallback. Selection is distinct from focus. Keyed DOM is an implementation choice.

requirements.title: Treat native semantics and announcements as a coherent projection
requirements.ears: WHEN a shell projection changes, the shell SHALL expose coherent native names, roles, states, relationships and actions for the current control identities, keeping preview imagery inert and keyboard focus distinct from selection.

scenarios.name: SOL04-02-scenario-1
scenarios.given: bar and popup show the same pending operation
scenarios.when: the matching refusal arrives twice
scenarios.then: both projections expose the same refusal state for the same control identity and focus remains on the user's control; announcement count follows ELM-ADOPT-012

scenarios.name: SOL04-02-scenario-2
scenarios.given: a preview image has retired while its restore control survives
scenarios.when: AT explores the control
scenarios.then: source state and supported action are available without an actionable image object or stale-incarnation activation

scenarios.name: stable-name-state-change
scenarios.given: a single-window group whose visible identity label is unchanged becomes active or pending
scenarios.when: native AT re-reads the control
scenarios.then: the accessible name remains aligned with the same visible label while state/description changes under the frozen naming policy

requirements.tradeoffs: One outcome owner requires lifecycle correlation and native speech/braille inspection; API availability differs by ABI.
requirements.guardrails: Control semantics plus actual native bridge required. Announcement ownership is separately ELM-ADOPT-012; multiple read-only status regions do not establish a single AT announcement. Keep the visible stable control label as the accessible name; expose transient state and action descriptions separately, within the frozen per-control naming policy. Verify cross-surface relationships in the native AT tree; DOM-local relationships do not automatically cross WebView documents.

requirements.title: Qualify composition as native field ownership
requirements.ears: WHILE an input method owns a shell field composition, the host SHALL preserve native preedit and candidate interaction, suppress shell handling of consumed keys, and accept commits only for the current field identity and composition generation.

scenarios.name: SOL04-03-scenario-1
scenarios.given: a launcher field has active preedit
scenarios.when: the input method consumes Enter to commit text
scenarios.then: the query receives the commit once and no launch occurs from that consumed key

scenarios.name: SOL04-03-scenario-2
scenarios.given: composition belongs to a retired field generation
scenarios.when: its delayed commit arrives after a new field takes focus
scenarios.then: neither field nor shell action receives the stale commit

requirements.tradeoffs: Native IME campaigns are costly; toolkit API examples cannot be transplanted across host lanes.
requirements.guardrails: Native field/composition epoch binds commits; consumed keys cannot trigger shell shortcuts. Native candidate/preedit and actual input target evidence required.

requirements.title: Preserve hierarchy and reachability under constrained geometry
requirements.ears: WHEN output geometry, text scale or label length changes, the shell SHALL preserve readable control names, visible focus, non-color state cues and keyboard-reachable actions using the frozen contrast, geometry and reflow policy.

scenarios.name: SOL04-04-scenario-1
scenarios.given: enlarged text and long localized labels on a small output
scenarios.when: the picker opens
scenarios.then: every action remains reachable and focused labels are legible according to the frozen oracle

scenarios.name: SOL04-04-scenario-2
scenarios.given: a popup owns focus on a removed output
scenarios.when: surviving-output recovery runs
scenarios.then: its declared fallback or rehosted scope is reachable and removed-generation input cannot activate controls

requirements.tradeoffs: Layout choices need measured geometry and AT bounds; freeze thresholds before qualification.
requirements.guardrails: Freeze measurable contrast/target/text/reflow budgets and test constrained outputs, long labels, scaling and non-color cues. Do not assume CSS tokens or screenshots establish native reachability.

requirements.title: Make action discovery agree with acknowledged outcomes
requirements.ears: WHEN a shell action is unavailable or unresolved, the shell SHALL expose the correlated reason and safe next step, retain eligible focus and controls outside its dependency domain, and never queue, defer or automatically replay input not accepted in that state or a rejected or Unknown action.

scenarios.name: SOL04-05-scenario-1
scenarios.given: a minimized generic application family is selected
scenarios.when: activation is refused natively
scenarios.then: it is not shown as restored, the reason and next action are reachable, and its preserved identity remains selected

scenarios.name: SOL04-05-scenario-2
scenarios.given: an operation has Unknown disposition and guidance was dismissed
scenarios.when: the user opens help or recovery with the keyboard
scenarios.then: guidance is available without resetting the desktop and reconciliation creates no automatic repeated mutation

scenarios.name: unrelated-observation-refresh
scenarios.given: a picker is open for a family
scenarios.when: an unrelated observation refresh completes with that family's dependency revision unchanged
scenarios.then: picker identity and focus persist and no new intent is emitted

scenarios.name: same-control-during-pending
scenarios.given: a native operation is Pending for a control
scenarios.when: the same control is activated again
scenarios.then: no second intent is emitted; one truthful not-accepted result is exposed under the frozen feedback policy without repeated announcement or later replay

requirements.tradeoffs: Shared vocabulary must follow native outcomes; no optimistic success or Unknown replay.
requirements.guardrails: Unrelated refresh means an unchanged declared family/target dependency domain and must preserve a valid picker/focus. Do not require concurrent native transactions. Repeated input during Pending follows INTERACTION.md feedback policy and ELM-UI-015; no second intent or announcement storm.

requirements.title: Stage-qualified feedback and physical presentation evidence
requirements.ears: WHEN an interaction stage is observed, the native authority and read-only projection SHALL label feedback, effect commitment, renderer submission, presentation and retirement separately, accepting physical completion only from identity-matched native evidence.

scenarios.name: Queued is not presented
scenarios.given: a matching image was decoded and a renderer queued a frame
scenarios.when: only image load or frameSwapped arrives
scenarios.then: presentation remains unproven and no physical-completion verdict is recorded

scenarios.name: Stale output presentation
scenarios.given: a transaction targets one output generation
scenarios.when: a presentation receipt arrives after hotplug changed that generation
scenarios.then: the receipt is retained diagnostically but cannot complete the replacement transaction

tradeoffs: Extra trace stages and correlation storage
Native feedback can approximate light output; independent hardware evidence is still needed
requirements.guardrails: Input, commit, rendering, presentation and retirement are separate stages. Record clock mappings, feedback flags and missing/discarded events. Frame callback/image-load/screenshot request is not hardware presentation.

requirements.title: Demand scheduling with bounded control liveness
requirements.ears: WHILE preview or observation demand exceeds admitted capacity, the bridge SHALL coalesce only replaceable observations within their identity domain, refuse unadmitted effects explicitly and preserve ordered cancellation, receipts and retirement capacity.

scenarios.name: Observation storm with cancellation
scenarios.given: preview queues are saturated within frozen byte and item bounds
scenarios.when: new observations and a cancellation arrive
scenarios.then: only semantically replaceable observations coalesce; cancellation and all retirement receipts remain deliverable in order

scenarios.name: Close during producer reservation
scenarios.given: a producer owns a reservation and the picker closes
scenarios.when: a late producer result arrives
scenarios.then: the closed demand remains cancelled and its existing owner/cleanup stays recorded; another authorized demand may use only independently available eligible capacity, never the held reservation before matching release

tradeoffs: Fairness and reserving control bytes reduce peak preview throughput
Coalescing requires explicit event taxonomy and atomic dependency preservation
requirements.guardrails: Coalesce only explicitly replaceable observations in the exact identity/dependency domain. Preserve reliable ordered effect/cleanup/control events, original deadlines and reserved progress capacity; no universal lossy stream.

requirements.title: Reversal and live reduced motion share native semantics
requirements.ears: WHEN motion is interrupted or the reduced-motion preference changes, the native renderer SHALL derive the successor from the last-presented geometry and preserve the same identity, cancellation, commitment and retirement rules under the approved motion profile.

scenarios.name: Reverse after an unpresented sample
scenarios.given: a restore has a queued sample newer than its last native presentation
scenarios.when: a minimize intent reverses it
scenarios.then: the successor starts from last-presented geometry under the native continuity rule and retires only the superseded generation

scenarios.name: Preference changes during capture
scenarios.given: a restore is awaiting a retained frame
scenarios.when: reduced motion becomes enabled before its matching frame arrives
scenarios.then: the approved reduced-motion route uses identical commit and cancellation obligations without replaying the effect or resetting its deadline

tradeoffs: Geometry and velocity continuity need native samples, not model time
The exact preference-switch policy must be frozen before qualification
requirements.guardrails: Native last-presented geometry/velocity and approved reversal profile. Reduced motion is a live native preference, with no velocity continuation/decorative motion under the selected reduced profile. Presentation timestamps, original38/34/52 cases remain required.
scenarioIDs: ELM-ADOPT-023 Reverse after an unpresented sample

requirements.title: Separate feedback latency and useful completion measurement
requirements.ears: WHEN host selection or release evaluation is prepared, the performance owner SHALL freeze same-machine workload budgets that separately measure input feedback, useful native presentation, whole-process resource closure and observer overhead, declaring missing stages.

scenarios.name: Missing presentation instrument
scenarios.given: a benchmark records CPU submission and feedback but lacks a presentation span
scenarios.when: the host comparison is evaluated
scenarios.then: unsupported spans are explicit and physical latency acceptance remains blocked rather than treating submission as presentation

scenarios.name: Observer hides tail failure
scenarios.given: a debug observer improves or perturbs scheduling
scenarios.when: the final benchmark packet is prepared
scenarios.then: paired observed and minimally observed runs expose overhead and all frozen workload thresholds are evaluated without discarding misses

tradeoffs: Hardware and minimally observed measurements cost time
Academic thresholds do not substitute for the frozen local budget contract
requirements.guardrails: No numeric limit invented from papers. Record latency distributions, missed frames, hardware/refresh/output metadata, CPU/memory/wakeups/idle-power and resource soak; QA observers disabled for product measurements.

requirements.title: Control delivery continuity distinct from proof identity
requirements.ears: WHEN authenticated control receipts are delivered, the bridge SHALL preserve their required per-channel causal order, detect gaps or regressions under the declared transport contract, reconcile uncertainty and keep repeated proofs idempotent without acknowledging unseen cleanup.

scenarios.name: reordered-cleanup
scenarios.given: Released and racing Cancelled proofs for a still-held job
scenarios.when: the later control event overtakes its prerequisite
scenarios.then: no unseen proof is acknowledged and no ownership is forgotten; the declared gap/reconciliation policy preserves cleanup

scenarios.name: cross-entry-proof-and-retry
scenarios.given: global proof IDs interleave across entries and a valid final Ack is lost
scenarios.when: a stable proof repeats on the authenticated delivery stream
scenarios.then: it does not create a false gap or duplicate physical cleanup; the declared idempotent acknowledgement/reconciliation policy can finish retirement

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: Use a separate delivery ordinal or independently qualified continuity mechanism. Proof IDs are not stream ordinals. Duplicate Acks may be retried idempotently when required; do not mandate withholding known-safe Ack retries. No global total order.

requirements.title: Capture must not starve native presentation
requirements.ears: IF a preview capture or export route exceeds its frozen presentation-impact budget on an active output, THEN the release verifier SHALL reject that route and retain a qualified alternative or explicit unavailable-preview state.

scenarios.name: cross-output-capture-impact
scenarios.given: restore motion on one output and capture demand on another
scenarios.when: the capture route runs on the measured hardware tuple
scenarios.then: presentation gaps and latency are measured on every active output against the same workload without capture

scenarios.name: over-budget-route
scenarios.given: measured route impact exceeds the frozen budget
scenarios.when: release admission evaluates it
scenarios.then: the route is rejected and the documented unavailable fallback is truthful; no stale or unqualified route substitutes for required capture acceptance

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: Synchronous compositor readback/encode is a concern, not a measured regression. Async readback/cropping/off-thread encoding need their own safety, fence, eligibility and ABI qualification. Unavailable fallback does not close mandatory source-stop/family gates.

requirements.title: Persistent demand converges to latest authorized source content
requirements.ears: WHILE authorized preview demand persists, WHEN tracked source content advances during outstanding capture, the provider SHALL retain bounded latest-revision demand and service it under the frozen pacing policy after eligible capacity returns, admitting none after closure or revocation.

scenarios.name: final-content-while-busy
scenarios.given: one admitted capture and multiple newer same-source revisions while visible demand persists
scenarios.when: the first job terminates and capacity returns
scenarios.then: bounded demand selects the latest valid revision without losing the final update or extending the first job deadline

scenarios.name: close-or-lock-before-followup
scenarios.given: a pending latest-content update
scenarios.when: demand closes, lock/revocation occurs or source identity changes before admission
scenarios.then: no unauthorized follow-up capture is admitted; existing jobs and cleanup obligations remain accounted

scenarios.name: continuous-change-and-final-revision
scenarios.given: authorized visible demand, continuously changing tracked content and eventually available eligible capacity
scenarios.when: the provider runs and then content change stops
scenarios.then: capture follows the frozen pacing policy, the final tracked revision is serviced when eligible, and presentation impact is measured under026 with no original deadline renewal

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: No forced allocation while backpressured/exhausted. Follow-up is a genuine new native-scoped request with its own original issued clock, not renewal of expired work. Control/retirement events are lossless. Pacing/refresh is frozen in the existing budget matrix before qualification; continuous change cannot create unbounded back-to-back capture. Latest revision is limited to native-tracked coverage, currently root-surface commits only; no subsurface/family fidelity expansion.

requirements.title: Source liveness and frame freshness are separate facts
requirements.ears: WHEN an authorized preview is displayed, the shell SHALL distinguish source liveness, captured content revision and frame age, and SHALL NOT describe historical or stale pixels as current content.

scenarios.name: live-source-with-old-frame
scenarios.given: a live source advances after its authorized frame was captured
scenarios.when: the old frame remains valid while a replacement is pending
scenarios.then: source liveness and frame age/freshness are distinguished; no false current-content claim or target substitution is made

scenarios.name: revocation-or-minimize
scenarios.given: a displayed frame and native source-state/lease update
scenarios.when: the source minimizes or lease revokes
scenarios.then: the existing historical/unavailable policy and native revocation govern display before replacement; no revoked pixels remain eligible

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: Refine labels only after reviewing the frozen historical/live/unavailable policy; do not relabel stale pixels as current-live or alter original13 S09 assertions.

requirements.title: Native keyboard entry and exit for the taskbar
requirements.ears: WHEN the declared taskbar-focus binding is admitted, the native host SHALL enter a bounded keyboard scope on the current output and retain the prior eligible application identity for the frozen exit/fallback policy, keeping the binding inert while locked.

scenarios.name: enter-and-escape
scenarios.given: an eligible application has focus and the taskbar is idle
scenarios.when: the declared conflict-resolved taskbar focus binding is invoked and then Escape ends the scope
scenarios.then: native keyboard and AT focus enter the bar and return under the frozen policy, with no unintended activation-history change

scenarios.name: retired-source-output-or-lock
scenarios.given: a bar keyboard scope whose prior application or output retires
scenarios.when: the scope exits or the session locks
scenarios.then: no replacement incarnation or removed output receives stale focus; the frozen eligible fallback/lock policy applies and idle bar does not intercept application input

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: This is native keyboard scope qualification, not a mandated permanent EXCLUSIVE mode or a new default shortcut. Declare which history changes are focus-only versus real accepted activation; do not override existing MRU policy.

requirements.title: Versioned disabled-action navigation policy
requirements.ears: WHEN a supported shell action becomes disabled, the shell SHALL retain its declared position, expose disabled state and any reason required by the frozen per-surface policy, and follow that navigation policy without dispatching it through pointer, keyboard or accessibility activation.

scenarios.name: supported-disabled-action
scenarios.given: a state change disables a supported menu action
scenarios.when: the user navigates with the declared per-surface policy
scenarios.then: the action position remains stable, native AT exposes unavailable state and reason, and attempted activation dispatches no effect

scenarios.name: all-disabled-and-focus-retirement
scenarios.given: all menu actions are disabled or the focused action becomes disabled
scenarios.when: navigation, Enter/Space or Escape occurs
scenarios.then: the frozen policy keeps focus and dismissal reachable without invoking a disabled action or trapping focus

requirements.tradeoffs: Additional protocol/evidence complexity must meet the frozen workload/resource budget. Reuse current modules and incrementally qualify changed paths.
requirements.guardrails: GTK and Windows/APG differ. Freeze the chosen per-surface policy; no universal requirement to focus every disabled control. Preserve existing right-click24 amendment and unsupported-action semantics.

originalSolCandidates.title: Versioned complete replay inputs with effect isolation
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a reducer replay is evaluated, the verifier SHALL reproduce state and ordered effect descriptions from the same versioned initial state and complete sanitized message history, while rejecting invalid replay input explicitly and executing no native mutations.
originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Fixture/schema upkeep and log bytes; preserve existing reducer rather than build another. Recorded timer inputs do not qualify native deadlines.

scenarios.name: Deterministic history
scenarios.given: A valid checkpoint and ordered native observations including deadlines
scenarios.when: The compiled reducer processes them twice
scenarios.then: All state/effect rows match and no effect endpoint is invoked

scenarios.name: Malformed racing clock input
scenarios.given: A pending request and envelope missing clock-domain metadata
scenarios.when: A late receipt is supplied through the envelope
scenarios.then: Validation fails explicitly; valid inputs retain original deadline and recorded order

originalSolCandidates.title: Proof-safe bounded history retention and compaction
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN retained records reach their configured bound, the authority SHALL reclaim only records whose safety obligations are preserved by retained proofs and replay floors, or explicitly refuse new admission while preserving unresolved and cleanup obligations.
originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Retention ownership table and compaction proof work; persistent sharing cannot make retained roots free; diagnostics may rotate independently.

scenarios.name: Expired replay after compaction
scenarios.given: A settled reclaimable record and retained replay floor
scenarios.when: Compaction completes and its old identity returns
scenarios.then: No mutation occurs and defined expired disposition is recorded

scenarios.name: Unknown and late cleanup
scenarios.given: Capacity pressure, Unknown request and outstanding consumer fence
scenarios.when: Diagnostics rotate and matching late receipt arrives
scenarios.then: Unresolved/cleanup obligations remain reconciled and charged storage is not freed prematurely

originalSolCandidates.title: Coherent recovery checkpoints and interrupted migration qualification
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN recovery installs a checkpoint, the authority SHALL validate its coherent schema, lifetime, watermark and retained obligations before effect admission, reconcile uncertain outcomes without replay, and preserve each original deadline.
originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Crash-barrier fixture maintenance and synchronous storage cost; a manifest over existing stores may suffice; database replacement is deferred.

scenarios.name: Completed checkpoint
scenarios.given: Synchronized checkpoint with Unknown and retired-request floors
scenarios.when: Frontend restarts
scenarios.then: Coherent observation/reconciliation state is restored without old mutation dispatch

scenarios.name: Interrupted migration
scenarios.given: Visible rename and incomplete synchronization/migration barrier
scenarios.when: Recovery sees newer scene plus late old-binding receipt
scenarios.then: Validated recovery completes or remains fail-closed without mixed owners, lost Unknown, or reset deadline

originalSolCandidates.title: Measured revision-bound derived caching
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHERE derived-state caching is enabled, the frontend SHALL return the same projection as uncached derivation for every accepted revision and invalidate cached results before using changed or retired dependencies.
originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Cache/index memory and invalidation bookkeeping may outweigh scan savings; adoption requires frozen-budget evidence, no invented thresholds.

scenarios.name: Unchanged dependency
scenarios.given: Pointer events with unchanged scene/query/policy revisions
scenarios.when: Taskbar groups are derived
scenarios.then: Output equals uncached oracle and measured recomputation improves under frozen workload comparison

scenarios.name: Identity reuse race
scenarios.given: Cached retired family incarnation
scenarios.when: Same label appears under new lifetime/incarnation during query change
scenarios.then: New identities govern derivation and action eligibility; stale family/preview authority does not survive

originalSolCandidates.title: Explicit concrete state and command refinement mapping
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN coupled replay is reported as conformance evidence, the verifier SHALL compare concrete state and ordered commands through a documented abstraction map and disclose stuttering, equivalence and environmental assumptions without substituting that evidence for native acceptance.
originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Mapping/comparator reviewer upkeep; full mechanized proof deferred; sampled exploration remains bounded evidence.

scenarios.name: Backend stuttering
scenarios.given: Broker housekeeping without observable frontend change
scenarios.when: Coupled replay applies declared abstraction map
scenarios.then: Frontend stutters while native accounting and eligible queued receipts remain checked

scenarios.name: Equal final state with incorrect effect order
scenarios.given: Executions with equal final visible model
scenarios.when: One reorders Cancel/Ack or retires before consumer completion
scenarios.then: Transition/command/resource comparison fails at first relevant mismatch

originalSolCandidates.title: Complete typed internal boundaries
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a validated external event enters an internal reducer, the controller SHALL carry domain-specific typed identities and outcomes through its resulting effect descriptions until wire encoding.

scenarios.name: Exact receipt
scenarios.given: a validated receipt for one request/incarnation
scenarios.when: the typed outcome is reduced
scenarios.then: only the exact transaction settles and wire encoding remains unchanged

scenarios.name: Foreign input
scenarios.given: a malformed or foreign-binding payload
scenarios.when: boundary validation runs
scenarios.then: no admitted event or mutation is produced and correlated refusal is retained

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Codec and call-site migration; phantom types do not authenticate senders; preserve wire bytes.

originalSolCandidates.title: Preserve effects as an auditable dependency algebra
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a native effect depends on another effect's completion, the controller SHALL admit the dependent request only after the matching native committed receipt satisfies the recorded prerequisite.

scenarios.name: Pending prerequisite
scenarios.given: restore-before-activate dependency for an exact incarnation
scenarios.when: restore remains Pending then its exact committed receipt arrives
scenarios.then: activation waits then registered activation can proceed

scenarios.name: Wrong prerequisite
scenarios.given: a refused restore or foreign committed receipt
scenarios.when: it arrives before activation
scenarios.then: it cannot satisfy the prerequisite and independent controls remain usable

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Explicit dependency metadata and replay oracle costs; retain independence; no new framework necessary.

originalSolCandidates.title: Publish one conversation contract with local obligations
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a protocol participant receives a control message, the system SHALL validate its actor, exact conversation identity and permitted transition before producing authority or ownership effects.

scenarios.name: Unadopted refusal
scenarios.given: an admitted reservation without storage
scenarios.when: the trusted producer refuses
scenarios.then: stable refusal proof preserves already-ordered cancellation proof

scenarios.name: Illegal retirement
scenarios.given: an adopted buffer or stale actor
scenarios.when: producer-refused or final-ack is supplied
scenarios.then: it cannot bypass drainage or retire current actor resource

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: New verification artifact refining existing behavior; manual table maintenance; no static-session-typing claim.

originalSolCandidates.title: Treat cancellation as a request followed by proved closure
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN cancellation invalidates an owned operation, the native authority SHALL reject subsequent unauthorized publication and retain its ownership record until matching physical retirement proof permits final acknowledgement.

scenarios.name: Cancel refusal race
scenarios.given: capture cancelled before adoption
scenarios.when: refusal completes asynchronously
scenarios.then: ordered cancellation/refusal proofs leave no reservation after final ack

scenarios.name: Held reader
scenarios.given: adopted buffer with held GIO reader
scenarios.when: cancel and shutdown occur
scenarios.then: fetch revoked immediately and terminal release waits for producer completion and reader drainage

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Retained records and native callback coordination; release on cancel-send unsafe; generation-scoped drain avoids global waits.

originalSolCandidates.title: Separate causal order, epoch identity and deadline time
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN queueing, frontend replacement or reconciliation occurs, the authority SHALL preserve the operation's original native clock domain, time origin and deadline while validating ordered control delivery independently of observation revisions.

scenarios.name: Restart receipt
scenarios.given: pending work and frontend restart
scenarios.when: exact late receipt arrives
scenarios.then: original request reconciles without deadline renewal or mutation replay

scenarios.name: Gap clock
scenarios.given: control sequence gap or replaced clock domain
scenarios.when: later delta/timeout arrives
scenarios.then: new admission withheld until coherent reconciliation and invalid timing cannot authorize work

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Metadata and clock/queue instrumentation; frontend timers feedback only; vector clocks unnecessary.

originalSolCandidates.title: preserve uncertainty in a structured reporting contract
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN an operation report is presented, the shell SHALL derive its message and available recovery actions from a validated correlated outcome and SHALL distinguish definitive refusal from Unknown without implying completion or authorizing replay.

scenarios.name: ERR-01-01
scenarios.given: an admitted restore with lost receipt
scenarios.when: transport disconnects
scenarios.then: the report states that completion is unconfirmed, preserves Unknown and offers no automatic repeat.

scenarios.name: ERR-01-02
scenarios.given: an exact unsent certificate and a simultaneous late receipt for a different request
scenarios.when: reports are reduced
scenarios.then: refusal is attached only to the certified request and the foreign receipt cannot alter its message or actions.

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: status-only messages are cheaper but obscure safe recovery; raw native messages reduce mapping work but leak details and blur semantics. Cost: category registry, compatibility review and differential fixtures. Validation: enumerate every existing outcome/recovery reason; every class has reviewed text and enabled-action oracle; corrupt or future reasons fail closed without fabricating a terminal outcome.

originalSolCandidates.title: one announcement owner and outcome-aware deduplication
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN an eligible correlated outcome transition requires attention, the controller SHALL publish one accessible status through the designated announcement owner, retain focus and suppress repeats of that outcome while preserving later distinct outcome transitions.

scenarios.name: ERR-02-01
scenarios.given: bar and popup projections on two outputs with stable focus
scenarios.when: the same refusal receipt is delivered repeatedly and a popup recreates
scenarios.then: one eligible announcement occurs and recovery detail remains reachable.

scenarios.name: ERR-02-02
scenarios.given: Unknown was announced and the original deadline has elapsed
scenarios.when: a valid late correlated receipt settles knowledge
scenarios.then: a distinct policy-eligible update is exposed without restarting the effect or changing its deadline; foreign-epoch receipts produce no such update.

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: per-view live regions are simple locally but duplicate output on multiple surfaces; one modal per failure interferes with focus and ordinary work. Cost: semantic routing, native AT integration and multi-output transcript qualification. Validation: count announcements against distinct eligible transitions, observe focus and speech/braille, include duplicate receipts and surface recreation. Preserve existing policy thresholds; freeze any missing quantitative oracle through S02/P0 rather than inventing one.

originalSolCandidates.title: bounded allowlisted diagnostics independent of authority
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHILE ordinary diagnostics are enabled, the diagnostics subsystem SHALL admit only allowlisted bounded records and SHALL report record loss without collecting excluded content or altering native authority, operation outcomes or deadlines.

scenarios.name: ERR-03-01
scenarios.given: a decoder failure containing a secret canary and window title
scenarios.when: a diagnostic record is produced
scenarios.then: only allowed category/context fields appear and neither canary nor title is retained.

scenarios.name: ERR-03-02
scenarios.given: diagnostic capacity is exhausted during a pending effect
scenarios.when: further records arrive and a terminal receipt races
scenarios.then: loss is observable, memory stays within the frozen budget and receipt settlement is identical to diagnostics-disabled execution.

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: unrestricted verbose logs simplify one incident at privacy/resource cost; aggregate-only metrics lose sequence context. Cost: event schema, producer audits and saturation tests. A ring buffer and separate counters are possible implementations, not mandated architecture. Validation: sensitive canaries across nested values and error strings; resource saturation, failure to write and malformed events preserve controller decisions. Measure log-rate, whole-process CPU/wakeups/memory, export cost and retention against `elm-performance/spec.md` ELM-PER obligations; the performance owner freezes numeric limits from P0 workloads before acceptance.

originalSolCandidates.title: recovery evidence distinguishes restored availability from past success
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a failed frontend or authority recovers, the shell SHALL report verified current availability separately from unresolved historical outcomes and SHALL admit new effects only after native reconciliation under the original deadline and identity contracts.

scenarios.name: ERR-04-01
scenarios.given: an admitted effect and crash before durable settlement
scenarios.when: a fresh epoch receives a coherent snapshot
scenarios.then: availability may recover while the previous effect remains unconfirmed and is never replayed.

scenarios.name: ERR-04-02
scenarios.given: a storage-full recovery failure and matching-looking geometry from a replacement incarnation
scenarios.when: reconciliation is attempted
scenarios.then: geometry alone cannot clear the historical reservation, no new dependent effect is admitted and the original recovery deadline remains enforced.

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: automatic retries may appear faster but are prohibited here; generic “recovered” banners omit the critical uncertainty. Cost: recovery phase/report integration and protected fault campaign evidence. Validation: original restore38/recovery34 with unchanged identity/oracle/deadline, held effects, missing/corrupt journal, unavailable storage, frontend/authority epoch replacement and stale proof. Component replay supplements rather than replaces native acceptance.

originalSolCandidates.title: explicit diagnostics export boundary
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN the user requests a diagnostic export, the shell SHALL produce an inspectable local bundle containing only validated export-allowed evidence and declared omissions, without exporting excluded content, sending it externally or modifying recovery authority.

scenarios.name: ERR-05-01
scenarios.given: diagnostics and an available core dump containing private memory
scenarios.when: the user requests the ordinary bundle
scenarios.then: the bundle includes allowed metadata and states that core/pixels/content are omitted.

scenarios.name: ERR-05-02
scenarios.given: export is assembling records while frontend epoch changes
scenarios.when: cancellation or disk-full occurs
scenarios.then: no success is reported, partial-artifact disposition is explicit, and neither old nor fresh recovery reservation is changed.

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: copying a journal manually is cheaper but produces unreviewable privacy and scope surprises; automated cloud uploads introduce unsupported product scope. Cost: bundle builder, accessible review and export fault testing. Validation: unpack and schema-check artifacts; canary and content scans; stale-epoch snapshot race, cancellation, disk-full and symlink/path defenses; measured export overhead must meet frozen performance budgets.

originalSolCandidates.title: Preserve control identity across publication and focus changes
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a presentation publication changes while a shell scope retains focus, the host SHALL preserve the focused surviving control identity, reject activation captured for retired or changed-scope identities, and apply the frozen eligible fallback only when that control is no longer eligible.

scenarios.name: SOL04-01-scenario-1
scenarios.given: Close is focused while another row is selected
scenarios.when: an unrelated catalog publication arrives
scenarios.then: Close keeps focus and the next activation invokes only Close

scenarios.name: SOL04-01-scenario-2
scenarios.given: an activation press belongs to a window incarnation and lease
scenarios.when: that incarnation retires and the row position is reused before release
scenarios.then: release dispatches no replacement action and eligible fallback remains reachable

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Identity propagation and native focus evidence; preserve identity rather than index or automatic selected-row refocus.

originalSolCandidates.title: Treat native semantics and announcements as a coherent projection
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a correlated shell outcome is presented on multiple projections, the shell SHALL expose its current control semantics through the native bridge and announce it once under the frozen interruption policy without changing keyboard focus.

scenarios.name: SOL04-02-scenario-1
scenarios.given: bar and popup show the same pending operation
scenarios.when: the matching refusal arrives twice
scenarios.then: one relevant refusal is announced, both projections show the same outcome, and focus remains on the user's control

scenarios.name: SOL04-02-scenario-2
scenarios.given: a preview image has retired while its restore control survives
scenarios.when: AT explores the control
scenarios.then: source state and supported action are available without an actionable image object or stale-incarnation activation

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: One outcome owner requires lifecycle correlation and native speech/braille inspection; API availability differs by ABI.

originalSolCandidates.title: Qualify composition as native field ownership
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHILE an input method owns a shell field composition, the host SHALL preserve native preedit and candidate interaction, suppress shell handling of consumed keys, and accept commits only for the current field identity and composition generation.

scenarios.name: SOL04-03-scenario-1
scenarios.given: a launcher field has active preedit
scenarios.when: the input method consumes Enter to commit text
scenarios.then: the query receives the commit once and no launch occurs from that consumed key

scenarios.name: SOL04-03-scenario-2
scenarios.given: composition belongs to a retired field generation
scenarios.when: its delayed commit arrives after a new field takes focus
scenarios.then: neither field nor shell action receives the stale commit

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Native IME campaigns are costly; toolkit API examples cannot be transplanted across host lanes.

originalSolCandidates.title: Preserve hierarchy and reachability under constrained geometry
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN output geometry, text scale or label length changes, the shell SHALL preserve readable control names, visible focus, non-color state cues and keyboard-reachable actions using the frozen contrast, geometry and reflow policy.

scenarios.name: SOL04-04-scenario-1
scenarios.given: enlarged text and long localized labels on a small output
scenarios.when: the picker opens
scenarios.then: every action remains reachable and focused labels are legible according to the frozen oracle

scenarios.name: SOL04-04-scenario-2
scenarios.given: a popup owns focus on a removed output
scenarios.when: surviving-output recovery runs
scenarios.then: its declared fallback or rehosted scope is reachable and removed-generation input cannot activate controls

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Layout choices need measured geometry and AT bounds; freeze thresholds before qualification.

originalSolCandidates.title: Make action discovery agree with acknowledged outcomes
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN a user discovers or invokes a shell action, the shell SHALL expose its frozen meaning and correlated outcome, preserve user context on refusal, and offer keyboard-reachable guidance and reconciliation without automatic replay of Unknown operations.

scenarios.name: SOL04-05-scenario-1
scenarios.given: a minimized generic application family is selected
scenarios.when: activation is refused natively
scenarios.then: it is not shown as restored, the reason and next action are reachable, and its preserved identity remains selected

scenarios.name: SOL04-05-scenario-2
scenarios.given: an operation has Unknown disposition and guidance was dismissed
scenarios.when: the user opens help or recovery with the keyboard
scenarios.then: guidance is available without resetting the desktop and reconciliation creates no automatic repeated mutation

originalSolCandidates.tradeoffs: Shared vocabulary must follow native outcomes; no optimistic success or Unknown replay.

originalSolCandidates.title: Stage-qualified feedback and physical presentation evidence
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN an interaction stage is observed, the native authority and read-only projection SHALL label feedback, effect commitment, renderer submission, presentation and retirement separately, accepting physical completion only from identity-matched native evidence.

scenarios.name: Queued is not presented
scenarios.given: a matching image was decoded and a renderer queued a frame
scenarios.when: only image load or frameSwapped arrives
scenarios.then: presentation remains unproven and no physical-completion verdict is recorded

scenarios.name: Stale output presentation
scenarios.given: a transaction targets one output generation
scenarios.when: a presentation receipt arrives after hotplug changed that generation
scenarios.then: the receipt is retained diagnostically but cannot complete the replacement transaction

tradeoffs: Extra trace stages and correlation storage
Native feedback can approximate light output; independent hardware evidence is still needed

originalSolCandidates.title: Demand scheduling with bounded control liveness
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHILE preview or observation demand exceeds admitted capacity, the bridge SHALL coalesce only replaceable observations within their identity domain, refuse unadmitted effects explicitly and preserve ordered cancellation, receipts and retirement capacity.

scenarios.name: Observation storm with cancellation
scenarios.given: preview queues are saturated within frozen byte and item bounds
scenarios.when: new observations and a cancellation arrive
scenarios.then: only semantically replaceable observations coalesce; cancellation and all retirement receipts remain deliverable in order

scenarios.name: Close during producer reservation
scenarios.given: a producer owns a reservation and the picker closes
scenarios.when: a late producer result arrives
scenarios.then: demand remains cancelled and the existing owner receives cleanup; no new capture is admitted until capacity is legitimately released

tradeoffs: Fairness and reserving control bytes reduce peak preview throughput
Coalescing requires explicit event taxonomy and atomic dependency preservation

originalSolCandidates.title: Absolute semantic deadline independent of paint scheduling
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN work crosses a queue, retry, frontend restart or paint suspension, the native authority SHALL preserve its original absolute deadline and start event; late exact outcomes SHALL reconcile uncertainty without extending acceptance or automatically replaying Unknown.

scenarios.name: Obscured frontend deadline
scenarios.given: the transaction has its original native deadline
scenarios.when: paint callbacks stop while capture is queued
scenarios.then: native expiry still occurs at that deadline and UI silence cannot extend the operation

scenarios.name: Late exact commit
scenarios.given: an operation became Unknown at its original deadline
scenarios.when: an authenticated exact commit receipt arrives later
scenarios.then: native truth is reconciled while the original deadline verdict remains a failure and no automatic replay occurs

tradeoffs: Requires native expiry independent of frontend updates
Late reconciliation and acceptance verdict are deliberately separate records

originalSolCandidates.title: Reversal and live reduced motion share native semantics
originalSolCandidates.ears: WHEN motion is interrupted or the reduced-motion preference changes, the native renderer SHALL derive the successor from the last-presented geometry and preserve the same identity, cancellation, commitment and retirement rules under the approved motion profile.

scenarios.name: Reverse after an unpresented sample
scenarios.given: a restore has a queued sample newer than its last native presentation
scenarios.when: a minimize intent reverses it
scenarios.then: the successor starts from last-presented geometry under the native continuity rule and retires only the superseded generation

scenarios.name: Preference changes during capture
scenarios.given: a restore is awaiting a retained frame
scenarios.when: reduced motion becomes enabled before its matching frame arrives
scenarios.then: the approved reduced-motion route uses identical commit and cancellation obligations without replaying the effect or resetting its deadline

tradeoffs: Geometry and velocity continuity need native samples, not model time
The exact preference-switch policy must be frozen before qualification

originalSolCandidates.title: Separate feedback latency and useful completion measurement
originalSolCandidates.ears: BEFORE host selection or release evaluation, the performance owner SHALL freeze measured same-machine workload budgets with separate input-to-feedback, input-to-native-presentation and resource-closure measures, stage coverage, observer overhead and missing-stage declarations.

scenarios.name: Missing presentation instrument
scenarios.given: a benchmark records CPU submission and feedback but lacks a presentation span
scenarios.when: the host comparison is evaluated
scenarios.then: unsupported spans are explicit and physical latency acceptance remains blocked rather than treating submission as presentation

scenarios.name: Observer hides tail failure
scenarios.given: a debug observer improves or perturbs scheduling
scenarios.when: the final benchmark packet is prepared
scenarios.then: paired observed and minimally observed runs expose overhead and all frozen workload thresholds are evaluated without discarding misses

tradeoffs: Hardware and minimally observed measurements cost time
Academic thresholds do not substitute for the frozen local budget contract
